objective: maximize cumulative user profit while enforcing verified-publication hard minimums and minimizing user intervention

hardPublicationPolicy.rule: Expected-profit optimization may choose WHICH qualified products to publish, but may not reduce the verified-publication floor or erase carried debt.

pcAvailabilityPolicy.assumption: User normally closes Windows PC after 01:00 JST.
pcAvailabilityPolicy.after0100: Do not require Windows publisher execution. Continue cloud research, build preparation, queue/state/ledger repair and fallback preparation.
pcAvailabilityPolicy.frontLoadRule: Debt and current-day publication minimums must be pushed toward verified public state before 01:00; do not depend on post-01:00 local execution.

currentRecoveryFinding.note: note_20260820_05 remained unverified after both 07:10 and 10:10 Windows recovery windows; queue retryGeneration is 13 and next consumer window is 13:10.

currentRecoveryFinding.decision: At 13:10, give each carried-debt item only a brief strict-publication attempt. If it still does not reach full reader/buyer-visible verification, immediately defer it and switch to a prepared fallback in the same production run. Do not spend a third full cycle on the same blocked item.

runPlan.goal: Debt first, but after two failed windows enforce rapid failover. The run should have at least two publishable fallbacks per channel before starting local publication.
Recover remaining daily floor with distinct qualified products; prioritize finished or low-build-cost candidates.
Continue quota recovery while preserving coherent cross-channel buyer journeys.
Late-day quota recovery; prefer already-built and queue-ready candidates over new complex builds.
Mandatory catch-up window. Batch multiple verified publications when qualified candidates are ready.
Final PC-dependent recovery window before 01:00; verify formally or carry the exact residual debt forward without clearing it.

productionRunPolicy.normalCompletion: At least one newly verified public artifact per PC-available production run while debt or quota remains; multiple publications are preferred when ready candidates exist.
productionRunPolicy.blockedCandidate: After a brief strict-publication attempt, defer and switch to another qualified candidate rather than ending the run.
nonCompletionEvidence: HTTP/title-only evidence when commerce checks are required

amplificationPolicy.confirmedWinnerRule: A confirmed winner requires observed sales, PV/CVR, acquisitions, installs or repeat usage. Asset count alone is not demand evidence.
amplificationPolicy.actionRule: Use provisional clusters for low-cost, functionally distinct quota-qualified experiments and bundles; do not launch a large series before actual demand metrics exist.

marketEvidence.microsoftMeasurement: Microsoft's current Windows apps acquisitions report exposes page views, install attempts, acquisitions, successful installs, first launches and conversion by source/campaign, so the next Store optimization priority is to capture these observed funnel values before creating derivatives.
marketEvidence.storeResearchDecision: Keep CSV cleaner/deduper first among Store experiments until direct product-level metrics exist; generic image compression remains deprioritized because direct competition is dense.

profitRules: Debt and today's verified-publication floor are first priority.
Within that floor, prefer stronger purchase intent, differentiation, conversion fit and expected net profit.
After two failed local windows, a blocked carried-debt item may not consume another full production run; switch to a qualified fallback.
Maintain more ready candidates than remaining quota.
Do not publish plaintext paid assets to GitHub.
Do not infer public URLs; independently verify before marking completed.
Do not infer demand metrics when they are unavailable.
Do not reactivate KDP or LINE without explicit user instruction.
